- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially >15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% of forecasted range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of past 10 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., >0.30), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for days 1–5 if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If true outcome shows volatility clustering (e.g., 3+ consecutive days with >5% deviation), model tends to smooth too much; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for next 3 days.
